rounds.text: Amar Vanijya Ltd is undergoing a profound structural turnaround that is currently masked by legacy top-line metrics. The most critical evidence of this transformation is the dramatic expansion in operating margins, which have improved by 260 percentage points over the last three years to reach -9% in March 2026 [E4]. This momentum is further validated by the most recent quarterly data, where operating margins surged to 40% compared to 29% in the year-ago quarter [E5]. The company is simultaneously strengthening its balance sheet by successfully reducing total borrowings to Rs 4.29 Cr as of September 2025 [E8]. These fundamental improvements support the signal that earnings growth is now accelerating [E17]. Conceded: the company faces significant headwinds with a 10-year compounded sales growth of -1% [E1] and a 21% decline in sales over the trailing twelve months [E2]. Despite these historical sales challenges, the shift toward profitability and debt reduction indicates a business model that is becoming increasingly efficient [E4, E5, E8].

Amar Vanijya Ltd faces a fundamental challenge as its long-term revenue trajectory remains stagnant, with compounded sales growth over the last decade at -1% [E1]. This decline has accelerated recently, evidenced by a -21% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months [E2] and a -12% year-over-year sales drop [E19]. The company’s profitability is equally concerning, as evidenced by a -150% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E3]. While the company has shown some recent improvement in margins, the trend remains unreliable, with both yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends classified as inconsistent [E6], [E7]. Conceded: the operating margin has improved by 260 percentage points over three years [E4], the quarterly operating margin increased by 11 percentage points year-over-year [E5], and borrowings have slightly decreased [E8]. Despite these isolated improvements, the persistent erosion of the top line and the volatility in margins suggest that the business lacks a stable foundation for sustainable growth [E1], [E2], [E6], [E7].

The bear focuses on historical revenue decline [E1], [E2], [E19], but ignores the critical pivot toward operational efficiency that defines the current trajectory. Conceded: compounded sales growth is negative [E1], [E2], [E19] and profit growth has suffered over the trailing twelve months [E3]. However, the bear dismisses the massive 260 percentage point improvement in operating margins over three years as isolated, failing to recognize this as a fundamental structural transformation [E4]. This momentum is confirmed by the most recent data, where quarterly operating margins expanded by 11 percentage points year-over-year [E5]. While the bear labels these trends as inconsistent [E6], [E7], the scanX signal engine identifies this as a clear case of earnings growth accelerating [E17]. Furthermore, the company is actively strengthening its balance sheet by reducing its debt burden [E8]. By prioritizing margin expansion and debt reduction over top-line volume, the company is demonstrating a disciplined shift toward sustainable profitability that the bear’s focus on historical sales growth fails to capture [E4], [E5], [E8], [E17].
